tweetMedia.transcription: So here's some news, but first, when you hear, let's say, show me your papers, or papers, what word comes to your mind? I think I know, and it's the same with me, okay? So with that in mind, let's get to the news. In Chicago, a 60-year-old man named Ruben Antonio Cruz, a legal and permanent resident of the United States, was stopped by ICE agents and given a ticket for one simple reason. He didn't have his immigration papers on him. He was sitting with a friend when ICE approached, asked for his proof of status, and when he said his documents were at home, they put him in a vehicle, drove around to verify his identity, and then issued him a $130 fine before letting him go. Now, guys, this isn't about immigration at this point. It's about a man who lives here legally in a sanctuary city being penalized for not carrying a piece of paper from a law written in 1940 during the World War II alien registration era, okay? And under that law, any non-citizen over 18 is technically required to carry their papers at all times. And it's rarely enforced, I mean, I guess until now. And that's the real story, guys. If ICE can't ticket a legal resident in Chicago for not having his papers, they can do it again anywhere and basically to anyone. Because once this kind of enforcement starts, it doesn't stay limited to one person or city. It's going to spread nationwide. something to keep an eye on
